title: Vow and Garden
premise: When pastry chef Lena Voss discovers her late grandmother's orchard deed names both her and Elias Marchetti—the man who walked out of her life seven years ago—as co-inheritors, she must share the failing farm with the one person she swore to forget. As they fight over the orchard's future, old betrayals surface: Elias left because Lena's mother forged documents that ruined his family, and the grandmother knew all along. To save the orchard from a predatory developer, they must expose her mother's corruption, forgive themselves for the lies they each told, and choose whether love is a debt or a gift. In the end, they sign the deed together—not as co-owners bound by obligation, but as partners who finally tell the whole truth.
about_author: Marguerite Joubert is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade between Provençal kitchens and Pacific Northwest orchards before turning to fiction. She writes romances about stubborn people, inherited land, and the recipes that outlive us.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Her café faces foreclosure; she works eighteen-hour days and insists her heart is 'a muscle like any other.' A lawyer's letter arrives: her grandmother has died and left her half of Bellwether Orchard. Emotional beat: exhaustion masking grief she refuses to feel.

chapters.title: The Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Lena drives to the orchard and finds Elias Marchetti already living in the farmhouse, equally stunned by the co-inheritance. They argue about selling immediately. Emotional beat: shock curdling into old resentment.

chapters.title: What He Left Behind
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashbacks to the night he vanished seven years ago—his father bankrupted, his name smeared—and why he never told Lena the reason. Emotional beat: guilt he's carried like a stone.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Conditions
chapters.summary: The will requires them to run the orchard through one full harvest season together or forfeit it to a developer, Halloran Group. Both refuse to lose to Halloran. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Working the trees side by side, they fall into an uneasy rhythm; she learns Elias stayed through his family's ruin alone. Emotional beat: grudging respect taking root.

chapters.title: Halloran Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: A slick representative offers each of them a buyout large enough to erase every debt. Lena is tempted; Elias refuses flatly. Emotional beat: money as a mirror of character.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Lena finds her grandmother's locked study and inside, correspondence suggesting the grandmother knew why Elias left. She hides the letters. Emotional beat: first crack in her certainty about her own family.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A storm traps them in the cider barn; nearly-kiss interrupted by his admission that he can't say why he left without destroying something. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by secrecy.

chapters.title: Mother's Visit
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Her mother, Diana, arrives uninvited, pressing Lena to sell and warning her away from Elias. Diana's control feels less like concern than fear. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Elias discovers in the county records that the document ruining his father bore a signature suspiciously like Diana Voss's. He says nothing to Lena yet. Emotional beat: truth as a loaded weapon.

chapters.title: Harvest Begins
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. The harvest brings the town together; Lena and Elias work in true partnership for the first time, and the almost-kiss finally happens. Emotional beat: joy neither trusts.

chapters.title: What the Letters Say
chapters.summary: Lena reads the hidden letters: her grandmother confesses she watched Diana forge the papers and stayed silent to protect her daughter. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Table
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Lena confronts him about what he knows; he admits the forgery accusation. She defends her mother, then falters. Emotional beat: trust fracturing along the fault line of blood.

chapters.title: Diana's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Diana files a legal challenge to the will, claiming the grandmother lacked capacity, aiming to seize the orchard and bury the forgery forever. Emotional beat: power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Alone, she admits her own sin: years ago she found a clue about the forgery and chose not to look, protecting her comfort over Elias's family. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness begins with honesty.

chapters.title: Elias Walks Again
chapters.summary: Elias, hurt by Lena's initial defense of Diana, packs to leave—repeating history. But at the gate he stops, realizing flight is how his family lost everything twice. Emotional beat: breaking the cycle.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Together they find the grandmother's ledger proving Diana's forgery and the grandmother's silence—a record meant to be found only when both heirs stood together. Emotional beat: the dead intervening through truth.

chapters.title: Standing Room
chapters.summary: At the capacity hearing, Lena testifies against her own mother, choosing truth over loyalty. Diana's challenge collapses; Halloran's option dies with it. Emotional beat: the cost of integrity, paid in full view.

chapters.title: What Forgiveness Isn't
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Mother and daughter speak honestly for the first time—no absolution, but no more lies. Elias realizes forgiveness isn't forgetting; it's refusing to let the wound decide for you. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Last of the Harvest
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The final crates go to press; the orchard turns its first real profit. Lena and Elias admit the heart was never containable after all. Emotional beat: surrender to love.

chapters.title: Two Signatures
chapters.summary: At the registry office they re-sign the deed as equal partners, then plant a new tree where the study once stood. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as choice rather than burden.

chapters.title: Vow and Garden
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. The café reopens with orchard fruit on the menu; Elias proposes not with a ring but with a grafted sapling—two varieties on one rootstock. Emotional beat: quiet, earned permanence.
